LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 5.3.1 PRESENT SIMPLE TENSE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Language Use 5.3.1 Present Simple Tense
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 5.3.1 Present Simple Tense, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: What do you do from morning to evening?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 5.3.1 Present Simple Tense together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy: learner connects using technology as they use the internet and other social media sites to watch a video on routine activities

and talk about the activities.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner appreciates and understands others as they talk about their routine activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Self-esteem is enhanced as learners apply present tense forms to talk about time and sequence of routine or daily activities.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Environmental Activities: as learners talk about time and sequence routine or daily activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Video clips, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist
